title: Api
description: A WeaveFFI API definition: one library's namespace.

version.description: The IR schema version this document targets (`0.13.0`).

doc.description: Documentation for the library as a whole, propagated to each package's top-level doc comment.

imports.description: Other IDL files whose declarations join this library's namespace, as paths relative to this file. [`crate::parse::load_api`] resolves them; a document assembled in memory has none.

records.description: Records: plain data types with named fields.

enums.description: Enums, C-style or with data-carrying variants.

errors.description: Error domains: named, open sets of error codes that callables report by naming the domain in their `throws`.

interfaces.description: Interfaces: reference-counted object types with constructors, methods, and statics.

callbacks.description: Callback interfaces: method sets the consumer implements and the producer calls.

RecordDef.description: A record: a plain data type with named fields, serialized across the ABI.

deprecated.description: A deprecation notice for the whole type.

fields.description: The fields, in declaration (and wire) order.

Field.description: A named field of a [`RecordDef`], an [`EnumVariant`], or an [`ErrorCode`].

type.description: The field type. Serialized under the key `type`.

TypeRef.title: TypeRef
TypeRef.description: A type, as a string: a primitive (`i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `f32`, `f64`, `bool`, `string`, `bytes`), a list (`[T]`), a map (`{K:V}`), an optional (`T?`), an iterator (`iter<T>`), or the name of a record, enum, interface, or callback interface.

EnumDef.description:
An enum: C-style when every variant is a bare discriminant, a sum type when any variant declares fields (see [`is_rich`](Self::is_rich)).

A C-style enum crosses the C ABI as an `int32_t`; a rich enum crosses serialized in a value buffer (an `i32` tag, then the variant's fields).

deprecated.description: A deprecation notice for the whole type.

value.description: The discriminant: the C-style value, or a rich enum's buffer tag. When absent it's one more than the previous variant's (`0` for the first).

fields.description: The variant's fields; non-empty makes the enum a sum type.

ErrorDomain.description:
An error domain: a named, open set of error codes that fallible callables report by naming the domain in their `throws`.

Code values are positive and unique within the domain. Domains are open: adding a code never breaks a deployed binding, which maps a positive code it doesn't know to the domain's base error type.

name.description: The domain name, which names the generated error type (for example `ContactError`).

doc.description: Documentation, propagated to the generated error type.

ErrorCode.description: A single named error within an [`ErrorDomain`].

code.description: The stable positive value carried across the C ABI.

fields.description: Payload fields the error carries beyond its code and message, serialized in the error's payload buffer.

InterfaceDef.description:
An interface: an opaque, reference-counted object type with constructors, instance methods, and static functions.

An interface value lives behind the FFI boundary and crosses it as a pointer that carries one strong reference; consumers see a class whose methods call into the producer. An interface value may appear anywhere a type can: as a parameter, a return, an iterator element, a record field, a list element, or a map value.

deprecated.description: A deprecation notice for the whole type.

constructors.description: Constructors: functions returning a new instance. A constructor declares no `return` (the instance is implicit) and isn't `async`.

methods.description: Instance methods, each called on an instance.

statics.description: Static functions namespaced under the interface.

Function.description:
A function exported across the FFI boundary.

The same shape describes a free function, an interface's constructors, methods, and statics (see [`InterfaceDef`]), and a callback interface's methods (see [`CallbackDef`]). The `async` and `cancellable` flags change how the symbol is lowered (a completion callback, an extra cancel-token parameter) without changing the parameters and return declared here.

return.description: The return type, or `None` for a function that returns nothing. Serialized under the key `return`.

doc.description: Documentation, propagated to the bindings' doc comments.

throws.description: How the function can fail: absent for a function that can't (any reported error is a producer bug), an error domain's name for one that reports that domain's codes, or `any` for one that fails with an untyped error (runtime code `-1` and a message).

async.description: Whether the function is asynchronous: it completes through a callback instead of returning. Serialized under the key `async`.

cancellable.description: Whether an async function accepts a cancel token.

deprecated.description: A deprecation notice, emitted as each language's deprecation marker.

type.description: The parameter type. Serialized under the key `type`.

Throws.title: Throws
Throws.description: What a fallible callable reports: the name of an error domain, or `any` for an untyped error (code -1 and a message).

CallbackDef.description:
A callback interface: a set of methods the **consumer** implements and the **producer** calls.

A consumer passes an implementation wherever the type appears as a parameter (bare, or optional as `Listener?`); the producer may keep it and call its methods from any thread. Methods are synchronous, may return any value type, and may declare `throws`.

deprecated.description: A deprecation notice for the whole type.

methods.description: The methods, in vtable order. Appending a method keeps every deployed binding working; reordering or inserting one doesn't.
